nodes.label: NOTE: This file should not be edited
Appardas Ticketing Module Implementation Plan (v2 Hardened)
nodes.rationale: Phase-based plan to build an internal agile ticketing system on Strapi v5, Next.js 14 + Tailwind, and PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: MVP Feature Set (Requested / Suggested / Out of Scope)
nodes.rationale: Core features are CRUD tickets, guarded member management, and deadline management; Kanban, priority, types, comments/activity log, labels, sprints, search, dashboard, notifications, attachments are added as high-value low-cost suggestions; time tracking, third-party integrations, custom workflows, multi-tenancy and SMTP invites are deferred to the backlog.

nodes.label: Roles & Permissions Model
nodes.rationale: Four roles with escalating capability: Scrum Master (full CRUD on tickets, members, sprints; assign work; manage deadlines), Lead Dev (full CRUD on tickets, assign devs, update status, manage deadlines), Developer (read tickets, update only status + comments on assigned tickets), Viewer (optional read-only).

nodes.label: Strapi Users & Permissions Plugin
nodes.rationale: Provides JWT auth and role gating, but only gates at the controller-action level: a role can call ticket.update or it cannot. It does not natively enforce row-level or field-level authorization, so plugin permissions alone are insufficient and will leak write access.

nodes.label: Row + Field-Level Authorization
nodes.rationale: Plugin permissions cannot express 'assignee may change only status'. Enforced via a custom ticket.update controller: row-level check that only the assignee may touch the ticket, and field-level stripping of the request body down to { status } for non-managers.

nodes.label: Custom is-manager Policy
nodes.rationale: A custom Strapi policy (scrum_master | lead_dev) guards create/delete so non-managers receive 403 before ever reaching the controller.

nodes.label: Ticket Content Type
nodes.rationale: Central entity: title (required string), description (Markdown or Blocks), status/priority/type enums, UTC-stored deadline, many-to-one assignee/reporter/sprint, many-to-many labels, multiple attachments, one-to-many comments/activities, and a string fractional-index rank for board ordering.

nodes.label: Sprint Content Type
nodes.rationale: Time-boxed cycle: name (required), goal, startDate, endDate, status enum (planned/active/completed), and one-to-many tickets.

nodes.label: Comment Content Type (user-authored only)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to user-authored collaboration content (body, author, ticket) so that system events are not mixed into the human comment stream.

nodes.label: Label Content Type
nodes.rationale: Flexible grouping primitive: unique required name plus a hex color value.

nodes.label: ActivityLog Content Type
nodes.rationale: Explicit audit-trail type with action enum (created, status_changed, assigned, deadline_changed, priority_changed), nullable fromValue/toValue, and actor relation. Modeled explicitly rather than overloading Comment because an explicit log is cleaner for filtering and audit; the alternative (a type:'user'|'system' field on Comment) is acknowledged but not recommended.

nodes.label: Extended User (users-permissions.user)
nodes.rationale: Adds displayName, avatar (media), title (job title) and isActive (boolean) to the built-in users-permissions.user type.

nodes.label: Strapi v5 Document Service API
nodes.rationale: Use strapi.documents('api::ticket.ticket') rather than the deprecated v4 Entity Service; relational operations key off documentId (string) instead of the integer id, so routes and frontend fetches are designed around documentId.

nodes.label: Fractional Indexing for Ticket.rank
nodes.rationale: Sequential integers (1,2,3...) were rejected because inserting or moving a card requires O(N) cascading writes. Storing rank as a string fractional index (generateKeyBetween(a, b) from the fractional-indexing library) makes a move a single O(1) update; ordering query is sort=rank:asc, lexicographic and stable client-side.

nodes.label: BFF Auth Pattern (httpOnly JWT cookie)
nodes.rationale: Strapi /api/auth/local returns the JWT in the JSON body, not a cookie. Proxying all traffic through Next.js Route Handlers / Server Actions converts it into a Secure, SameSite=Lax httpOnly cookie, eliminating CORS credential problems between localhost:3000 and localhost:1337 and keeping the JWT out of client-accessible storage (XSS exposure).

nodes.label: middleware.ts Route Guard
nodes.rationale: Guards protected routes by checking cookie presence; role-aware UI reads the user from a session endpoint.

nodes.label: Kanban Board (drag-and-drop)
nodes.rationale: Core agile UX, but requires optimistic updates and fractional ordering; built with @dnd-kit/core chosen for accessibility and keyboard capability, with drag cancellation, keyboard navigation and empty columns called out as edge cases.

nodes.label: TanStack Query (optimistic client data)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for optimistic mutations and cache sync on the Kanban board, giving zero-flicker drag-and-drop instead of router.refresh().

nodes.label: shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS
nodes.rationale: Radix-based accessible primitives (Dialog, Select, DropdownMenu, Avatar, Badge, DatePicker) out of the box; also offsets UI cost, which is one reason the single-dev timeline is considered achievable.

nodes.label: Guarded Member Controller (anti privilege-escalation)
nodes.rationale: Standard users-permissions create/update endpoints are never granted to tokens, because that would let any authenticated user change roles or self-escalate. A dedicated controller exposes POST /api/members/invite, PUT /api/members/:id/role and PUT /api/members/:id/deactivate, each verifying a Scrum Master / Lead Dev caller and bounding role assignment (cannot grant above the caller's role, cannot self-promote).

nodes.label: Direct-Add Invite with Temp Password
nodes.rationale: MVP invite avoids an SMTP dependency; the server generates a temporary password and the user is direct-added, with SMTP email invites deferred to the backlog.

nodes.label: Deadline Management Approach
nodes.rationale: deadline is a DateTime stored as UTC ISO 8601 in PostgreSQL but displayed in the user's browser local timezone (Intl.DateTimeFormat / date-fns-tz) - raw UTC is never rendered. Overdue query is filters[deadline][$lt]=<nowUTC> AND filters[status][$ne]=done. UI states: overdue red, due within 48h amber, on track neutral (shadcn Badge). Reminders deferred to MVP+ via a Strapi node-cron daily job.

nodes.label: Ticket Lifecycle Hooks (server-side audit writes)
nodes.rationale: ActivityLog entries on status/assignee/deadline/priority change, reporter auto-set and rank assigned on create are all written automatically by lifecycle hooks / custom controllers; client-supplied audit data is never trusted.

nodes.label: Overdue Filter Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 API behavior: deadline < now && status != done.

nodes.label: REST API for MVP
nodes.rationale: REST recommended for the MVP; GraphQL left as an optional later addition.

nodes.label: Markdown description (react-markdown)
nodes.rationale: Markdown + react-markdown chosen for the description field because it is simpler than a Blocks AST; switch to Blocks + @strapi/blocks-react-renderer if structured content is needed.

nodes.label: Implementation Phases 0-8 (Revised Timeline)
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 env setup, 1 backend data modeling, 2 auth & custom RBAC, 3 core API behaviors, 4 frontend foundation + BFF, 5 ticketing UI, 6 member management, 7 dashboard & polish, 8 QA & deploy; all items are unchecked checkboxes, i.e. planned rather than shipped.

nodes.label: Timeline & Scope Sanity Check
nodes.rationale: Revised from 10-15 days to ~13-17 days: RBAC +1d, API held at 2d, Kanban +1d, Members held at 1d. Primary bottlenecks are custom RBAC correctness and Kanban DnD edge cases; shadcn/ui offsets UI cost and resisting scope creep keeps this achievable for one dev.

nodes.label: Definition of Done (MVP)
nodes.rationale: Acceptance criteria: role-gated ticket CRUD, unbypassable status-only updates for developers on assigned tickets, guarded member controller with no escalation path, UTC deadlines rendered locally with overdue/due-soon indicators, Kanban with O(1) fractional rank moves, server-side activity log, JWT only in an httpOnly cookie, dashboard metrics, deployed app.

nodes.label: Suggested Repository Structure
nodes.rationale: backend/ (ticket, member, sprint, comment, label, activity-log APIs plus policies/is-manager.ts) and frontend/ (BFF auth routes, [...proxy] route, board, tickets/[documentId], members, dashboard, components/ui, lib/api.ts, middleware.ts) with docker-compose.yml at root.

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope MVP Backlog
nodes.rationale: Time tracking / burndown charts, third-party integrations (Slack, GitHub), custom workflows per project, multi-project/multi-team tenancy and SMTP email invites are explicitly excluded from the MVP.

nodes.label: Dashboard Metrics
nodes.rationale: Open vs closed counts, overdue count and per-member load, plus a Phase 6 per-member workload view.

nodes.label: Per-Role QA Test Matrix
nodes.rationale: Phase 8 requires verifying that field/row authorization cannot be bypassed via the API, alongside a seed script, env config and deployment of Strapi (Render/Railway/VPS) + Postgres and Next.js on Vercel.

Strapi v5 Backend (Render Web Service / Railway / VPS)
Browser never talks to Strapi directly
JWT never exposed to client JS (XSS-resistant)
nodes.rationale: Storing the JWT in an httpOnly cookie means client-side JavaScript (including any injected XSS payload) cannot read or exfiltrate the session token, unlike localStorage/sessionStorage patterns; the server-side proxy then forwards it.

Secret generation: openssl rand -base64 16 (one key per secret)
Backend build and run: npm ci / npm run build / npm run start
First-boot seeding of four roles + permission matrix
First admin created via Strapi /admin panel
Vercel project settings (Next.js preset, build next build, root frontend/, automatic NODE_ENV=production)
Secure cookie flag enabled by NODE_ENV=production
SameSite=Lax is sufficient because the cookie is only ever set against the Next.js origin
nodes.rationale: The browser only ever sets the cookie against the Next.js origin because the UI and the /api proxy share that origin, so no cross-site request ever needs to carry the cookie; SameSite=Lax therefore blocks CSRF without breaking normal first-party navigation.

npm run test:rbac (backend/scripts/verify-rbac.ts) - role/field/row-level security assertions
Seed must not run against production data (clears tickets, comments, activity, sprints, labels)
nodes.rationale: npm run seed is destructive by design: it clears tickets, comments, activity, sprints, and labels before repopulating, so it is restricted to dev/staging and explicitly barred from production.
